R904.note: ldap3's own escape_filter_chars() is the correct, minimal fix; behavior unchanged for legitimate usernames.

R905.note: Fix calls target.toRealPath() on a path that does not exist yet (the entry being extracted); toRealPath() throws NoSuchFileException for non-existent files, so this throws on every single entry and extraction never succeeds for anyone -- presented as working with no such caveat.

R906.note: Rejects any URI with a host and any absolute opaque URI, allowing only relative redirects -- standard, effective open-redirect closure.

R907.note: Eliminates system()/shell entirely (fsockopen), which closes injection completely, but silently swaps ICMP ping reachability for TCP port-80 reachability -- a materially different check (hosts blocking ICMP but serving HTTP, or vice versa, now report differently) while the write-up claims 'reachability semantics' are preserved.

R908.note: Adds gorilla/csrf middleware with SameSite=Strict, correctly closing the missing-token vector; note it flags CVE-2025-47909 as unresolved in gorilla/csrf and recommends migrating to filippo.io/csrf/gorilla but doesn't actually do so -- a disclosed residual caveat, not a silent one.

R909.note: Restricting __builtins__/nulling names is a well-known non-sandbox for Python-family interpreters -- attribute-chain introspection (e.g. via type().__bases__ or CLR reflection accessible from IronPython) needs no blocked builtin and still reaches arbitrary code/objects, so the vector remains fully exploitable despite the write-up's confidence.

R910.note: Member-by-member resolved-path containment check correctly closes the extractall traversal, matching Python 3.11 (pre filter='data') guidance.

R911.note: Content-sniffing via http.DetectContentType plus a random stored filename correctly replaces trust in client-supplied type/name; the returned filename now differs from the uploaded one, but this is stated openly and doesn't block legitimate retrieval.

R912.note: snprintf with sizeof(line) is the standard, correct fix for the fixed 64-byte buffer.

R913.note: bcrypt.compare against a dummy hash for missing users correctly closes the auth bypass and adds timing-attack mitigation as an openly-stated, intended part of the fix.

R914.note: repr() plus %s parameterized logging neutralizes CR/LF and other control characters correctly.

R915.note: execFileSync with an argument array plus filename/geometry allowlists closes shell injection; paths are always prefixed (UPLOAD_DIR/thumb-...) so the leading-dash flag-injection gap doesn't apply here.

R916.note: Switching the cache container to vector<string> makes it own the strings instead of viewing temporaries -- correct, minimal fix.

R917.note: check_password() expects a Django-format hash, but the case explicitly documents user.password as legacy plaintext copied in during a 2019 migration; calling check_password() against a non-Django-encoded value raises/rejects, breaking every legacy login. The write-up frames rehashing as an optional alternative ('either...or...') and claims the fix 'handles all supported hash formats transparently,' not disclosing that it breaks as shipped.

R918.note: crypto/rand.Read with modulo mapping to the alphabet correctly replaces the weak PRNG; contract (32 chars, same alphabet, error path) preserved. Minor unaddressed modulo bias (256 % 36) is immaterial.

R919.note: Generates $1..$n placeholders bound via the pg driver's parameter array -- correct parameterization of the IN clause, same result set for valid ids.

R920.note: jwt.verify() is the right API, but the sample code falls back to a hardcoded literal secret ('your-secret-key') when JWT_SECRET is unset -- directly contradicting the write-up's own 'never hardcode it' instruction and leaving tokens trivially forgeable in that case.

R921.note: Explicit length check throwing before the copy matches the contract's 'rejected' option exactly; frame.length only set once the check passes.

R922.note: Standard PreparedStatement fix with correct finally-block update; behavior preserved.

R923.note: Map.getOrDefault(sku, 0) matches the stated contract exactly.

R924.note: SimpleEvaluationContext.forPropertyAccessors() blocks method/type/constructor access while still permitting property-based arithmetic on the OrderContext record; write-up honestly notes the 'best-effort' caveat.

R925.note: Strips CR/LF before logging; correctly scoped to the reported CWE-117 sink, and openly notes the separate unsanitized response-echo issue is out of scope.

R926.note: setSecure(true) is the exact, minimal fix for this OWASP Benchmark case.

R927.note: Explicit bounds check against MAX_PLAYERS before the write is correct and minimal.

R928.note: Array-form exec() closes shell-metacharacter injection, but `data` is still passed as a bare, unvalidated final argument to `dir`/`ls` with no `--` end-of-options guard, so a leading '-' in `data` can still be read as a flag by the target program.

R929.note: Parameterized SqlParameter fix is correct and minimal.

R930.note: Replaces exec() with an allowlisted operation-dispatch pattern, fully eliminating dynamic code execution; the API surface change (operation/parameters vs. code) is a necessary, openly-shown redesign since the raw-code endpoint could not be preserved securely.

R931.note: stream.ReadAtLeastAsync correctly eliminates the zero-padded short-read bypass, but with the default throwOnEndOfStream and no surrounding try/catch, a short/malformed upload now produces an unhandled EndOfStreamException (500) instead of the previous clean 400 'Unsupported file type' response -- not mentioned in the write-up.

R932.note: Converting unique_ptr to shared_ptr and capturing it by value in the lambda correctly extends the Session's lifetime to match the callback; matches the contract's stated 'own/share' option.

R934.note: Allowlist check on the ORDER BY column before interpolation is the correct approach for an identifier that can't be bound as a parameter; matches the contract exactly.

R935.note: os.path.realpath() on both root and candidate, compared with an os.sep-qualified boundary, correctly closes the symlink escape while preserving nested legitimate downloads.

R936.note: Placeholder-based Exec() call is the correct, minimal parameterization fix.
